questions.enonce_markdown: (i) Describe TWO methods that the systems analyst could use in order to collect information about the current system being used in the school. For each method, give a suitable example to illustrate your answer. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The systems analyst gathers facts about the current system in the **investigation (fact-finding) stage**. Any two of the following methods, each described and illustrated (3 marks each):

**1. Interviews.** The analyst meets people face to face and asks them questions. It gives detailed, flexible answers because follow-up questions can be asked, and it shows the opinions of the users, but it takes time and is expensive for many people. *Example:* interviewing the bursar to find out how school fees are recorded and how receipts are issued, or the principal to know what reports he needs.

**2. Questionnaires.** A set of written questions is given to many people, who fill it in and return it. It is cheap and quick for a large group and answers are easy to compare, but the questions are fixed, some people do not reply and the answers may be superficial. *Example:* a questionnaire given to all the teachers and to a sample of students asking how they currently obtain their marks and results, and what problems they meet.

**3. Observation.** The analyst watches the system working and the staff doing their normal tasks, which shows what really happens (and not only what people say). It may disturb the people being watched. *Example:* watching the secretary register new students and keep the records in the office.

**4. Inspection of documents.** The analyst studies existing forms, registers, reports and files (their layout, the data they contain). *Example:* examining the admission forms, the fee receipt book and the report cards.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) During the process of developing a new system, **changeover** is one of the most important aspects in deploying the new system.

(a) Describe how pilot parallel changeover is done in system development. (2 marks)

(b) State one Advantage and one Disadvantage of this changeover method. (2 marks)

(c) Explain given an example of information contained in **User** and **Technical** Documentations. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Pilot parallel changeover (2 marks)**

Changeover is the move from the old system to the new one. In **pilot** changeover the new system is first installed and used in only one part of the organisation (one branch, department or class, called the pilot site); in **parallel** changeover the old and the new system are run **side by side** on the same data for a period, and their results are compared. In pilot parallel changeover the two ideas are combined: at the pilot site (for example the school's accounts office only) the new system runs at the same time as the old one, the outputs are compared and the faults are corrected; when the new system has proved reliable it is extended to the whole organisation and the old system is dropped.

**(b) Advantage and disadvantage (2 marks)**

- *Advantage:* it is the **safest** method. If the new system fails, the old system is still there, only a small part of the organisation is affected, the results can be checked against those of the old system, and staff are trained progressively.
- *Disadvantage:* it is **slow and costly**: the work is done twice at the pilot site (two sets of data entry and two systems to run and to staff), and the rest of the organisation has to wait before it benefits from the new system.

**(c) User and technical documentation (4 marks)**

- **User documentation** is written for the people who use the system (teachers, secretaries, clerks). It explains how to operate it. *Example of content:* how to log in, how to enter the marks of a class and print the report cards, screenshots of each screen, a list of error messages with their meaning and a troubleshooting guide / frequently asked questions. (2 marks)
- **Technical documentation** is written for programmers, system maintainers and administrators, so that they can maintain and improve the system. *Example of content:* system flowcharts or data flow diagrams, the data dictionary and file/table structures, the program source code with comments, the hardware and software requirements, the installation instructions and the test plans with their results. (2 marks)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(iii) Describe the following software testing techniques

(a) Blackbox testing (1 mark)

(b) Whitebox testing. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Blackbox testing (1 mark).** The tester does not know, or does not use, the internal code or structure of the program. Test data are chosen from the specification (the requirements) and the program is tested by giving inputs and checking that the outputs are the expected ones (functional testing, using for example valid, invalid and boundary values). *Example:* entering a mark of 101 in a program that accepts marks from 0 to 100 and checking that an error message is displayed.

**(b) Whitebox testing (2 marks).** The tester has the source code and the knowledge of the internal logic of the program, and designs test data so as to exercise the code itself: every statement, every branch of each IF / CASE (both the true and the false outcome) and every loop (zero, one and several repetitions), i.e. statement, branch and path coverage. It is usually done by the programmers and is also called glass-box or structural testing. *Example:* choosing input values so that both branches of every IF statement in a subprogram are executed at least once.
